title: Triangle Four Centres
summary: Centroid and circumcentre from three vertices; orthocentre from Euler’s line. ~90 bytes.

body.text: AfterSchool lists this as the other DSE must-enter program next to 2×2 linear systems. Enter vertices (A,B), (C,D), (X,Y). Four pauses: centroid Gx, Gy, then circumcentre Ox, Oy. Orthocentre is H = 3G − 2O (Euler: G divides OH in 2 : 1). Incentre is the side-length weighted average of the vertices.

body.label: Memory / run mode
body.text: ~90 bytes of the shared 680-byte pool. Create the slot in COMP, Deg. Type ? → : ◢ Goto Lbl If Then from SHIFT 3 (P-CMD).
Question: Use this program to solve the case: Vertices (4, 3), (0, 0), (4, 0).
Given: Right-angled at (4, 0). Hypotenuse from (0, 0) to (4, 3).

items: 【EXE】 → Ox = 2. 【EXE】 → Oy = 3/2  (circumcentre, midpoint of the hypotenuse)
Orthocentre H = 3G − 2O = (4, 0), the right-angle vertex. Incentre I = (3, 1)

body.text: Question: Use this program to solve the case: Vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 3).
Question: Use this program to solve the case: Collinear points.

items: G still prints (the average). Circumcentre hits Math ERROR (denominator 0). That is the ‘not a triangle’ signal

body.label: Pitfalls
body.text: If two points share a y-coordinate the circumcentre formula can hit Math ERROR — enter a point with a distinct y first. Long published listings (~227 bytes) also print incentre, circumradius, and the circumcircle equation using SD memories.
